source.title: Alveolar osteitis associated with methicillin-resistant Staphylococcus epidermidis

extraction_metadata.scope_note: Atoms represent independently reviewable assertions from the supplied case report. Background claims attributed to cited literature were not converted into primary-study findings. No cefixime or azithromycin dose, route, or frequency was invented. All model-extracted atoms remain needs_review because no independent human reviewer step is represented.

atoms.canonical_statement: The report aimed to suggest that systemic antibiotics may have insufficient efficacy during alveolar osteitis, especially when a multidrug-resistant organism is involved.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The aim of this report is to suggest that systemic antibiotics may provide insufficient efficacy during alveolar osteitis

atoms.canonical_statement: The case involved a 35-year-old woman with right mandibular posterior pain and no reported systemic pathologies.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: A 35-year-old female presented to a dental office with a chief compliant of pain in the right mandibular posterior region.

population.label: Single 35-year-old female dental patient described in the case report

atoms.canonical_statement: The patient reported starting cefixime on her own two days before presentation without improvement.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: two days before she had independently begun treatment with cefixime without any improvement

population.label: Single 35-year-old female dental patient described in the case report

exposures.details: Self-started two days before presentation; dose, route, and frequency were not reported.

atoms.canonical_statement: Pain was spontaneous and radiated from the right mandibular region to the right ear; percussion and cotton-roll occlusal testing provoked pain only at tooth 4.6.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Pain was described as spontaneous and irradiating from the right mandibular region up to the right ear

population.label: Single 35-year-old female dental patient described in the case report

outcome.definition: Clinical localization of pain to tooth 4.6 by symptom pattern and bedside dental testing.

atoms.canonical_statement: Preoperative radiography showed no periradicular bone resorption, periapical radiolucency, visible decay, or restoration infiltration, but showed an ill-defined radiotransparent area around the pulpal chamber of tooth 4.6.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: No periradicular bone resorption or periapical radiolucencies were appreciable.

population.label: Single 35-year-old female dental patient described in the case report

atoms.canonical_statement: Tooth 4.6 was extracted after root separation and luxation; the socket underwent mechanical debridement and saline irrigation, followed by collagen sponge placement and crisscross suturing.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: An accurate alveolar revision was performed with mechanical debridement of granulation tissue and subsequent intra-alveolar irrigation with sterile saline solution rinse.

exposures.details: Rizectomy/root separation, luxation, root extraction, debridement, saline irrigation, collagen sponge, and crisscross suture.

atoms.canonical_statement: The collected sample was cultured on Columbia blood agar, McConkey agar, mannitol salt agar, and Tryptic Soy broth at 37 degrees C for 24 to 48 hours, with Columbia blood agar also incubated anaerobically and microaerobically.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: The collected sample was cultured in 5% Columbia blood agar (CBA), McConkey agar, Mannitol salt agar, and Tryptic Soy broth

atoms.canonical_statement: Bacterial identification used Gram staining and API Staph biochemical testing; the isolate was also screened for mecA with a specific PCR assay.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Bacterial species identification was performed by Gram staining technique and biochemical tests (API Staph System

atoms.canonical_statement: Kirby-Bauer susceptibility testing assessed erythromycin, azithromycin, clarithromycin, trimethoprim-sulfamethoxazole, enrofloxacin, ciprofloxacin, gentamicin, doxycycline, mupirocin, and amikacin, with interpretation by CLSI 2021 clinical breakpoints.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: using the Kirby-Bauer method, and the results were interpreted with Clinical and Laboratory Standards Institute (CLSI) clinical breakpoints

atoms.canonical_statement: Four days after extraction, alveolar osteitis was diagnosed in the setting of persistent spontaneous pain, loss of the alveolar clot, gingival inflammation, and socket tenderness, with no purulent drainage and no radiographic abnormality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Diagnosis was alveolar osteitis, and the immediate management was suture removal and irrigation of the socket

population.label: Single 35-year-old female dental patient described in the case report

outcome.definition: Post-extraction diagnosis based on persistent pain, absent clot, gingival inflammation, and painful socket examination four days after extraction.

atoms.canonical_statement: At the four-day post-extraction visit, the patient also had a palpable right submandibular lymph node; the socket had no purulent drainage and radiographs showed no abnormality.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: Four days after extraction, the patient referred persistence of spontaneous pain not responsive to analgesic therapy and the appearance of a palpable lymph node

atoms.canonical_statement: Alveolar osteitis management included suture removal and socket irrigation with sterile saline plus 1:1 hydrogen peroxide, followed by topical antiseptic gel and intra-alveolar chlorhexidine 0.20% rinses.

population.label: Single 35-year-old female dental patient described in the case report

exposures.details: Suture removal, saline plus hydrogen peroxide irrigation, topical antiseptic gel, and intra-alveolar chlorhexidine 0.20% rinses.

atoms.canonical_statement: The authors concluded that systemic antibiotics seem to have limited efficacy in the management of alveolar osteitis.

source_anchor.verbatim_excerpt: the administration of systemic antibiotics, as evidenced in the literature and in our case, seems to have limited efficacy

atoms.canonical_statement: When antibiotic administration is judged necessary, the authors advised dentists to consider antimicrobial resistance and a history of antibiotic abuse or misuse, and to consider changing antibiotic class or category.
